source.title: Nonlinear Initialization Methods for Low-Rank Neural Networks
source.authors: Kiran Vodrahalli; Rakesh Shivanna; Maheswaran Sathiamoorthy; Sagar Jain; Ed H. Chi

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents reading.
record.tranche_reason: Reports experiments training low-rank ResNet-50 and EfficientNet models and measures downstream validation accuracy under different initialization methods and rank scales. Those results bear on initialization and width conditions, but it does not measure training classification error, so evidence is only a conceptual test of parts of V4.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training loss convergence only for its layerwise initialization optimizer and validation accuracy for downstream ImageNet training. It does not report the networks' training classification error. Its low-rank approximation objectives and cited initialization findings are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses established full-rank initialization recipes to construct low-rank initializations and evaluates its methods through ImageNet validation accuracy and layerwise function approximation. These outcomes do not test V4's training-speed, signal-propagation or trainable-depth claims, or any other version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that nonlinear function-matching initializations tend to improve downstream generalization over spectral initialization, with modest gains and similar implementation cost. They report a positive empirical association between better initialization function approximation and better generalization; they do not establish faster classification training or greater trainable depth.
record.recipe_differences: Trains low-rank ResNet-50 and EfficientNet on ImageNet using SGD with momentum, comparing initialization approaches; evaluates downstream top-1 accuracy rather than training classification error. Initialization-objective optimization uses Adam.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported accuracy varies with rank scale, architecture width, and regularization method. Authors say gains are more apparent at smaller rank scales, while width effects are mild in their tested regime.

fits_no_version.finding: Nonlinear low-rank initialization typically improves final ImageNet validation accuracy over baseline or spectral initialization, with exceptions across architectures, rank scales and regularization choices. The authors report an average gain of about 0.3 percentage points.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Matching nonlinear layer functions at initialization can improve downstream generalization of low-rank ImageNet networks.

fits_no_version.finding: For EfficientNet-b7 at rank scale 0.10, reducing layerwise approximation error during initialization is associated with improved downstream validation accuracy. The reported four-epoch convergence concerns initialization fitting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Better layerwise function approximation at initialization is associated with better final validation accuracy in the tested low-rank network.

fits_no_version.finding: The theoretical results bound spectral initialization's suboptimality for a nonlinear approximation objective, with larger gaps at smaller ranks and increasing input dimension under specified width assumptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Spectral parameter approximation can be suboptimal for matching ReLU layer functions, depending on rank, dimension and width.

record.problems: The study does not report training classification error, the target measure of the main claim. Most model-comparison results are downstream ImageNet validation accuracy. Experiments use three random seeds; the paper reports standard errors up to one standard deviation. The EfficientNet comparison suggests width effects are mild in the tested regime, which the authors attribute to width being likely linear in input dimension.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying rows: the reported downstream accuracy and initialization-objective convergence do not measure training classification error or the speed of classification training named by the versions. The initialization-objective convergence statement is in Section 4.1.2; ImageNet accuracy results are in Tables 1–8 and Sections 4.2–4.3.

untested.parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including random or corrupted labels and model-size or regularization effects.
Spurious-minimum frequencies in realizable two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and the effect of extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth in plain networks and its prevention by residual shortcuts or special initialization.
Whether activation-matched initialization preserves signals and gradients, accelerates network training or increases trainable depth; orthogonal-versus-Gaussian comparisons.
Recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics and threshold-related divergence.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, including Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's V4 status from tested_not_extracted to not_tested. Empty result rows are appropriate for these claim versions. EfficientNet divergence during Frobenius-decay tuning does not test V5 because no stability threshold or curvature dynamics are measured.

versions.untested_parts: No CIFAR training classification error, corrupted or random labels, model-size sweep for fitting, early stopping, or training-error comparison.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment or spurious-minimum frequency measurement.
No plain-versus-residual depth comparison or training-error outcome.

The study compares initializations and rank scales in low-rank ResNet-50 and EfficientNet models, with downstream ImageNet validation accuracy, but does not report training speed or training classification error as a result. Its stated convergence within six epochs concerns fitting the layerwise initialization objective, not training the classification network.
No learning-rate stability threshold, loss rise, curvature, sharpness, or divergence experiment.
No batch-normalization comparison or normalization-speed measurement.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
